instructions.candidate: You have 8 minutes to take a focused history from this patient who presents with a headache. You may ask questions and should demonstrate appropriate communication skills. At the end, you will be asked about your differential diagnosis and immediate management plan.
instructions.examiner: Patient presents with sudden onset of severe headache, described as 'worst ever', starting 1 hour ago. Observe candidate's communication skills, systematic approach to history taking, and ability to identify red flags.
instructions.standardizedPatient: You are a 45-year-old man experiencing a sudden, severe headache (10/10) that started 1 hour ago while you were at work. The pain is like a 'thunderclap'. You feel nauseous and have vomited twice. You have no significant medical history and are not on any medications. You are worried because you've never had a headache like this before.

criteria: Identifies subarachnoid hemorrhage as likely diagnosis

instructions.candidate: You have 8 minutes to take a focused history from this patient who presents with abdominal pain. You may ask questions and should demonstrate appropriate communication skills. At the end, you will be asked about your differential diagnosis and immediate management plan.
instructions.examiner: Patient presents with severe, constant, and generalized abdominal pain. Observe candidate's communication skills, systematic approach to history taking, and ability to identify red flags.
instructions.standardizedPatient: You are a 40-year-old chef. You have been experiencing severe, constant abdominal pain for the past 6 hours. The pain started in the central abdomen and is now more generalized. You have not passed gas or had a bowel movement since the pain started. You have a history of peptic ulcer disease. You drink socially and do not smoke.

redFlags: No bowel movements or gas passage

references.title: BMJ Best Practice: Acute abdominal pain

instructions.standardizedPatient: You are a 65-year-old retired teacher experiencing sudden breathlessness. You have felt short of breath for about 3 hours, and it has worsened over time. Family history of respiratory or cardiac disease
